Provision trial Dedicated cluster for benchmarks

Follow-up to confirm success criteria and timeline

Marcus Diaz - Prepare benchmarking scripts, sample prompts, and infra setup instructions - due 2026-04-12

summary: POC scoping for Lark Systems focusing on integration planning: SDKs, OpenAI-compatible endpoints, function/tool calling, and structured output. Discussed success criteria (latency p95, throughput/QPS, cost targets, accuracy/regression), benchmark plan (latency/throughput/concurrency/cache), timeline (2-4 week pilot + ramp), infra options (hosted vs Dedicated vs Private/VPC), security requirements, and next steps to provision trial infra and run benchmarks.
header:
Date: 2026-04-08
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Diaz (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Lark CTO), Evan Brooks (Lark Platform Eng), Sofia Martinez (Lark ML Eng)
transcript:
00:00 Avery Chen: okay good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining. this is Avery from Redwood Inference. we have Marcus from our infra team as well. can you hear me ok?
00:06 Priya Nair: yes loud and clear, thanks.
00:09 Marcus Diaz: hi all, hey Priya, Evan, Sofia.
00:12 Evan Brooks: hey.
00:14 Avery Chen: quick agenda - scope POC success criteria, run through your workload sizing and sample prompts, propose benchmark plan, and talk integration surface: SDKs, OpenAI-compatible endpoints, function/tool calling and structured output. any other items?
00:26 Priya Nair: nope that's it, main thing for us is latency and cost - we have live traffic with tight SLAs so want to see realistic numbers.
00:33 Sofia Martinez: and the structured JSON outputs matter; we need deterministic fields for downstream parsers.
00:38 Avery Chen: great. maybe start with you sharing the workload and SLOs?
00:42 Evan Brooks: sure. so baseline, our prod e2e qps for the Lark assistant is about 120 requests per min during peak - so roughly 2 requests/sec sustained; peaks up to 12 rps for short bursts. average prompt length is ~350 tokens in, 200 tokens generated. 95th latency target for user-facing flows is <600ms, but for higher complexity flows we can accept up to 900ms. budget-wise we want to test to stay under our internal target of $X per 1k tokens, we'll share exact numbers offline.
01:12 Marcus Diaz: just to clarify, is that 200 tokens gen on average or max?
01:16 Evan Brooks: average. some flows go to 800 tokens generation.
01:20 Priya Nair: and reliability is key; if latency spikes we need graceful degradation.
01:24 Avery Chen: understood. for the pilot we usually run two classes of benchmarks: latency p50/p95/p99 at target concurrency and throughput tests for sustained qps. we'll also do a cost/throughput estimate using our quantized variants. does that sound aligned?
01:37 Priya Nair: yes. can you run both hosted and Dedicated comparison? we want to see fallbacks.
01:42 Marcus Diaz: absolutely, we can provision a small Dedicated pool with the same model family and compare to hosted. for private deploys we can also do a VPC-connected private plane but that'll add setup time.
01:52 Sofia Martinez: question about integration - we want to keep our current OpenAI-compatible client code. do you support OpenAI-style endpoints and function calling?
01:58 Avery Chen: yes, Redwood provides OpenAI-compatible endpoints and SDKs. function calling is supported; we also have structured output enforcement via JSON schema and output validators. small caveat - some models require post-processing for strict schema adherence but we provide tool-assisted reranking and constrained decoding options to improve determinism.
02:18 Sofia Martinez: that's promising. is function calling identical to OpenAI? any differences?
02:22 Marcus Diaz: it's compatible for the common patterns - we support function call hinting, explicit call responses, and streaming. differences are mostly in the telemetry/tracing fields and optional headers we expose for routing.
02:33 Evan Brooks: good. about the SDKs - language support? Node, Python, Java?
02:37 Avery Chen: official SDKs in Python and Node; Java community client and REST endpoints work for any language. we can share code samples for your stack.
02:44 Priya Nair: on security: we need KMS integration and audit logs, SOC 2, and SSO with SAML. how's that handled?
02:51 Marcus Diaz: Redwood Private and Dedicated both offer customer-managed KMS/HSM via cloud KMS integrations, plus audit logs and SOC 2 attestation. SAML SSO and RBAC are supported at the org level. we'll share our security pack.
03:03 Priya Nair: great. timeline? we need a 2-4 week POC ideally.
03:07 Avery Chen: typical POC has three phases: week 0-1 onboard & infra + share sample data, week 1-2 run benchmarks and tuning, week 3 analyze results and iterate; many customers wrap up in 3 weeks if dependencies are quick.
03:20 Evan Brooks: ok that works. what are success criteria - can we write a concrete list?
03:24 Avery Chen: yes. propose: 1) p95 latency < 600ms for 90% of critical flows - that's primary. 2) sustained throughput at target QPS with <5% error/retry rate. 3) cost per 1M tokens within your internal target (TBD). 4) Structured output accuracy - JSON schema pass rate > 95% on sample test set. 5) Security signoffs for VPC/KMS. does that capture it?
03:49 Priya Nair: yes, add regression threshold - e.g., generation quality metrics shouldn't drop more than 5% on our eval prompts.
03:56 Sofia Martinez: we'll provide a labeled set of 200 prompts for the schema and quality tests.
04:01 Avery Chen: perfect. for benchmarks we'll need: sample prompts, exemplar responses for quality evals, expected concurrency patterns, and a traffic replay script if you have one.
04:11 Evan Brooks: we can share a sanitized dataset and a small traffic replay script.
04:15 Marcus Diaz: on the technical side, we'll run two model configs: full-precision host and a quantized variant to measure cost tradeoffs. we'll also enable KV/prefix caching for conversational flows to measure hit rates.
04:28 Priya Nair: how do you measure cache effectiveness? Sofia?
04:31 Sofia Martinez: we typically check prefix overlap and cache hit ratio across sessions; if your assistant frequently repeats context we should see high hit rates.
04:39 Avery Chen: noted. any constraints on infra? e.g., network egress or blocked ports?
04:44 Evan Brooks: our environment requires outbound to Redwood endpoints, SAML SSO, and we prefer VPC peering for Dedicated trial.
04:51 Marcus Diaz: VPC peering is fine; it adds a day or two for infra setup.
04:56 Priya Nair: about logs - we need per-request tracing and token-level cost breakdowns for analysis.
05:01 Marcus Diaz: we provide token-level cost and latency breakdowns in the Console and via an API. we can give you sample traces.
05:09 Sofia Martinez: function-calling reliability: if the model misformats the function call payload, do you have a recovery mechanism?
05:15 Avery Chen: yes, we have structured output validators and can auto-invoke post-call retries or rerank results using constrained decoding; SE team can tune prompts and tools.
05:25 Evan Brooks: benchmarking specifics - can you run p95 with warm KV cache and cold cache? we want both numbers.
05:31 Marcus Diaz: absolutely, we'll run warm and cold cache scenarios and report both.
05:35 Avery Chen: also measuring burst scaling - we'll do a step-load test to your peak spike pattern.
05:40 Priya Nair: do you support canary model rollouts and fallback to smaller models on degradation?
05:45 Marcus Diaz: yes, rollout policies and automatic fallback to compatible model variants are supported. you can set routing rules by latency or error rate.
05:53 Sofia Martinez: when running the POC, will the OpenAI-compatible endpoints require code changes?
05:57 Avery Chen: minimal. most customers change only the base URL and add our API key header. function call semantics remain the same. we'll share migration snippets.
06:06 Evan Brooks: can Redwood collect metrics to feed into our Grafana?
06:09 Marcus Diaz: yes we have a metrics exporter and webhooks; Prometheus style metrics are available.
06:14 Priya Nair: good. about data retention and logs, we need to ensure PII is not logged.
06:18 Avery Chen: we support config for data retention policies and can disable logging of user content for the Dedicated trial. we'll include that in the security docs.
06:27 Sofia Martinez: any limitations on structured output size? we produce nested JSON up to a few KB.
06:32 Marcus Diaz: structured responses that size are fine; very large payloads can hit token limits but for usual use-cases it's okay. we'll note token budgets in the benchmark.
06:40 Evan Brooks: ok next - timeline to get a trial cluster?
06:44 Marcus Diaz: we can spin a small Dedicated cluster in 48-72 hours after NDA and network info. Hosted benchmarks can start earlier.
06:51 Priya Nair: we should sign NDA today, i'll have our legal ping yours.
06:55 Avery Chen: perfect, we'll send the POC doc and NDA link.
06:58 Priya Nair: great. any concerns about model fidelity? we have custom finetuned models that need to be supported.
07:04 Avery Chen: we can host custom model artifacts on Dedicated or Private deployments; we'll discuss artifact upload and registry steps in the POC doc. there is a slightly longer setup for private on-prem artifacts.
07:15 Sofia Martinez: for the evaluation, can we test function calling where the function returns strongly-typed JSON and then check schema conformance programmatically?
07:22 Marcus Diaz: yes, we'll run an automated test harness that validates schema and reports pass/fail per sample and a pass rate.
07:29 Evan Brooks: what about streaming? we need partial tokens for UI rendering.
07:33 Avery Chen: streaming is supported; you'll get token-level events and latency to first token metrics.
07:37 Priya Nair: any hidden costs for telemetry or longer retention?
07:40 Avery Chen: telemetry retention beyond default is an add-on; we'll call it out in pricing.
07:44 Sofia Martinez: we also need retries behavior documented - e.g., idempotency keys and how to handle partial results.
07:50 Marcus Diaz: we'll share best practices including idempotency keys, backoff strategies, and how to use the SDK helpers.
07:58 Evan Brooks: final items - for the bench, please include a checklist of what you need from us.
08:03 Avery Chen: yes checklist: sanitized prompts, expected QPS and spike pattern, labeled eval set, network access details, SSO contact, and sign-off on SLA targets. we'll put that in the POC doc.
08:13 Priya Nair: about success criteria again - can you include a quality regression test with a threshold?
08:18 Avery Chen: yes we will include automatic quality regression checks on the 200-sample set; threshold set to <=5% regression vs your baseline.
08:26 Sofia Martinez: ok good. anything else?
08:29 Evan Brooks: I have one question on cost calc: will you provide both per-token and projected monthly run costs under expected qps?
08:34 Marcus Diaz: yes, we provide per-token cost, per-request average, and a projected monthly spend estimate for your traffic profile.
08:41 Priya Nair: timeline recap?
08:43 Avery Chen: action items: we'll send POC proposal + pricing + checklist by Friday (2026-04-10). Evan will share traffic profile and dataset by 2026-04-09. Marcus will prep benchmark scripts and spin Dedicated trial by 2026-04-12. follow-up meeting to review results scheduled for week of 2026-04-20.
08:57 Priya Nair: that works. thanks everyone.
09:00 Avery Chen: thanks, we'll follow up with docs and the NDA link. talk soon. bye.
09:05 (call ends)
